subject.title: fix(firecrawl): require own legacy provider config entries

question: Should Firecrawl ignore inherited legacy properties on programmatically supplied `OpenClawConfig` objects even though normal JSON/JSON5 and include paths cannot produce that state?
rationale: The patch is mechanically safe, but deciding whether inherited properties are malformed input, a supported programmatic contract, or behavior that should be normalized generically requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Require supported ingress proof
options.body: Pause merge until a real plugin or runtime path that preserves inherited nested config is demonstrated, then retain the narrow Firecrawl guard and live proof.

options.title: Declare inherited config unsupported
options.body: Explicitly define inherited configuration properties as unsupported and decide whether enforcement belongs at a generic config boundary rather than only in Firecrawl.

options.title: Pause speculative hardening
options.body: Close or defer both overlapping implementations if no supported or observed path can produce the state.

recommendation.title: Require supported ingress proof
recommendation.body: Pause merge until a real plugin or runtime path that preserves inherited nested config is demonstrated, then retain the narrow Firecrawl guard and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership across Firecrawl configuration and extension test infrastructure, making this the best available routing candidate for the contract decision.
